outline.purpose: Trace request, helper, schema, component, and persistence ownership only through packages/web/src/app/dashboard/preferences/page.tsx:fetchPreferences; packages/web/src/app/api/user/preferences/route.ts:GET. Separate code-backed behavior from source-backed recommendations.

outline.purpose: Explain the normal path and compatibility boundaries for react fetch error state test. Convert repository branches into named fixtures with complete observable outputs.

outline.purpose: Compare fetch outcome, response status, parsed data, loading state, displayed defaults, error signal, and retry or navigation behavior. Include the planned table, explain every row, and cite the repository source for each expected result.

outline.heading: Step-by-Step Default state after fetch error Procedure
outline.purpose: Present the numbered procedure for default state after fetch error: Render the authenticated preference page with deterministic initial defaults. Control GET outcomes for success, non-OK, rejection, and malformed data. Wait for loading completion and assert switch values, disabled states, and visible feedback. Navigate away and back to detect stale state or unhandled promise warnings.

outline.heading: Nextjs client fetch testing: Assertions and Diagnostics
outline.purpose: Cover nextjs client fetch testing with status, state, side-effect, call-count, and visible-output assertions. Explain the failure signal a CI report must retain.

outline.heading: What Regressions and Boundaries Prevent False Confidence?
outline.purpose: Retained defaults can look like a successful load, so the test must also assert loading completion and the intended error signal. List nearby concerns owned by related articles and define the post-change cases that remain in scope.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.purpose: Answer five to eight questions in 40 to 60 words each. Cover "How do you test loading completion and retained defaults when the preference page receives an error or rejected fetch?" plus question variants based on react fetch error state test, preference page loading test, failed settings request ui, default state after fetch error, nextjs client fetch testing.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.purpose: Summarize the verified contract without introducing new claims, then use this CTA: Exercise GET failures on the preference page and keep loading plus default-state assertions in the browser post-flow.
